Since \(BQ\) and \(BP\) are the two trisectors of angle \(B\), the angle between them is one-third of \(\angle B\):

\[
\angle QBP=\frac{\angle B}{3}=14^\circ
\]

So

\[
\angle B=42^\circ
\]

Given \(\angle A=39^\circ\), we get

\[
\angle C=180^\circ-39^\circ-42^\circ=99^\circ
\]

Now \(P\) is the intersection of the trisectors nearer to side \(BC\). Therefore,

\[
\angle PBC=\frac{\angle B}{3}=14^\circ
\]

and

\[
\angle BCP=\frac{\angle C}{3}=\frac{99^\circ}{3}=33^\circ
\]

In triangle \(BPC\),

\[
\angle BPC=180^\circ-14^\circ-33^\circ=133^\circ
\]

The answer is \(133^\circ\).
